manifest.deal: Deal before reading on: python3 <SKILL>/scripts/deal.py dreamlike-button.metadump.json (<SKILL> is the metadump skill's folder) prints your hand, an angle to start from and two deep cuts, and writes a dealt copy: the user's words and don'ts, tier 1 and the review questions, plus a random half of everything else, in a fresh order. Work from that copy: read whole and as stored, this file pulls every session toward the same shape.
manifest.prompt: a button with custom bezier curve hover state animations that makes it feel dreamlike and ethereal, but practical for a website
how_to_read: 1. Deal first: python3 <SKILL>/scripts/deal.py dreamlike-button.metadump.json, then read the dealt copy it names for every step below (write-backs go to this file).
2. Read the head: the first 35 lines hold manifest, essence and routing (Read limit=35, or jq '{manifest, essence, routing}' dreamlike-button.metadump.json).
3. Pick the route for your job and run its jq: jq '<routing[i].jq>' dreamlike-button.metadump.json
4. Also pull the anti-keywords and review prompts (checks) for your scope: jq '.anti_keywords, .checks' dreamlike-button.metadump.json
5. Look up any term (lowercase): jq '.index["<term>"]' dreamlike-button.metadump.json  -> hits give id + path; not_meant lists senses to avoid.
6. Grep works too: every entry is one line, so grep -n '<word>' dreamlike-button.metadump.json returns whole entries.

7. When you have built something that renders, look at it before you finish: python3 <SKILL>/scripts/look.py <your file.html> screenshots it, hovers and opens it, and lists clipping, overlap and overflow. Read the screenshots and fix what you see.

essence.one_sentence: A hover feels dreamlike when it keeps moving after the pointer has arrived, and the light that spreads past the edge is what carries that motion; the label, the focus ring and the press are the ground the control stands on while it moves.
essence.summary: A hover that keeps moving after it looks finished, a glow that spreads past the edge over a translucent fill, and a label, focus ring and press that hold up for keyboard, touch and reduced-motion users.

formula.full: hand-chosen cubic-bezier motion (settle, float, slow enter or breath) + opacity-faded glow layer behind the box + translucent fill with the label held by a contrast layer or a solid plate + visible focus ring and press state
formula.essential: a moving hover over a glow that spreads past the edge, with the label held legible

roles.curve: the motion: how the move lands, floats or breathes, chosen per button
roles.glow: the light past the edge that makes the button read as ethereal
roles.fill: a translucent fill so the page shows through; the label is held legible by a contrast layer (look-label-contrast) or a solid plate, and both readings stay open
roles.focus ring and press: the practical part that keeps the control working without a pointer
roles.reduced-motion fallback: keeps the colour and glow response with the travel removed

angles.text: Start from one fast settle with a long low tail: the hover arrives at once and the tail carries the last of the move, with the glow following it.
Start from a float that keeps moving while the pointer is held: the lift drifts a few pixels on a slow loop, so the hover reads as floating rather than landing.
Start from a cool light past the edge: a moonlight-blue glow spreads 8 to 12px beyond the box, the fill stays translucent, and the label sits on a plate the glow cannot wash out.
Start from a breath: at rest the glow rises and falls slowly, and a press cuts the breath short and answers at once.

poles: a glow that spreads past the edge
a label held at 4.5:1 on the brightest point of the glow
a tail that keeps moving after the pointer settles
feedback that lands within a quarter second

llm_brief.text: On the table: the user's words, quoted: "a button with custom bezier curve hover state animations that makes it feel dreamlike and ethereal, but practical for a website". Motion: a hand-written cubic-bezier() per button, from a fast front with a long low tail, a slow start that drifts in over 1.2 to 2.4s, or a symmetric glide; feedback 120 to 250ms, settle 500 to 1200ms, float and breath loops 2.4 to 8s; transform and opacity move on the compositor, and the glow is an opacity-faded pseudo-element, since box-shadow repaints each frame. Look: a glow spreading 8 to 12px past the edge at full strength, in moonlight blue, lamp amber, or the fill's own light; a translucent fill at 0.2 to 0.3 alpha with the page pattern showing through, the label held by look-label-contrast (a solid plate or a text-shadow halo). Practical: a 3px focus ring offset from the edge, 3:1 against the glow (focus_ring_spread); a 24 by 24 CSS px box with the glow outside the measure; press feedback at 50 to 100ms (press-timing), and a reverse from the current value when the pointer leaves mid-settle (reverse-mid-transition); no hover stuck after a tap; a reduced-motion block that keeps colour and glow and drops the travel, float and breath. Ways in: the settle (a fast front, a long low tail that carries the feel); the float that keeps going (a 4 to 8px lift that moves while held); eerie cold glow (a cool light spreading like moonlight past the edge, the label on its plate); one breath at rest (a slow rise and fall, cut short by the press). None is the default. Dials: the curve as a spread (front-loaded tail, late arrival, symmetric glide, or a pop at y 1.3 to 1.5); enter 120 to 250ms for a quick answer or 1.2 to 2.4s for an arrival, exit 250 to 450ms; glow from 0.3 opacity at 8px blur to a saturated rim 8 to 12px out. Worn paths: the usual move is a 0.2s ease fade; fresher: a hand-written curve with a long tail. The usual move is translateY(-2px) with a grey shadow; fresher: a glow in the button's own light past the edge. The usual move is a neon glow; fresher: light tinted from the fill or moonlight blue. The usual move is a faint halo; fresher: a glow that gains strength to full hover. The usual move is animating width, top or box-shadow; fresher: transform and opacity with a faded glow layer. The usual move is removing the outline; fresher: a 3px focus ring. Open: brand colours and target size are not given; Penner-style curve values were not retrieved; hover under reduced motion is inferred; the 3:1 focus figure is from WCAG 1.4.11, not fetched; plain CSS is assumed.

ak-pr-hover-only-label.instead: label visible at rest; hover adds the glow around it

ak-pr-dim-label.instead: label held at 4.5:1 at the glow's brightest point; glow spreads around the label

ak-pr-outline-removed.term: outline removed for a cleaner look
ak-pr-outline-removed.instead: a visible focus-visible ring, or the glow at full strength as the focus cue

ak-pr-layout-animation.term: animating width, top or box-shadow on hover
ak-pr-layout-animation.instead: transform and opacity; glow as an opacity-faded pseudo-element

ak-pr-full-motion-no-fallback.term: full float with no reduced-motion block
ak-pr-full-motion-no-fallback.instead: a reduce block that drops travel and keeps the colour and glow change

ak-sense-shirt-button.instead: clickable web control on a page

ak-sense-physical-button.instead: clickable web control on a page

ak-sense-mac-button.excluded_sense: macOS window control or a Mac mouse button

ak-sense-ease-preset.excluded_sense: a single named preset such as ease

ak-sense-page-load.excluded_sense: animation that runs once when the page loads
ak-sense-page-load.instead: motion while the pointer is over the button

ak-sense-practical-cap.excluded_sense: a cap on how dreamy or glowing the button can be
ak-sense-practical-cap.instead: keeps the button legible, focusable, tappable and smooth

ak-hover-default-ease.instead: a hand-written cubic-bezier with a slow drift and a long soft settle that keeps moving after the pointer arrives

ak-sense-surreal.excluded_sense: a dream-sequence cut or a glitch in the motion
ak-sense-surreal.instead: slow drift and float as the motion; the uncanny skew stays open as one reading the consumer may choose

ak-pr-press-filter.instead: a practical press: transform and opacity only, with the blur layer pre-rendered and fixed so the button stays smooth

ak-sense-ghostly.instead: for search, the sense of ethereal: light, airy, translucent; the eerie reading stays open for image and copy

ak-lift-grey-shadow.instead: a glow in the button's own light, spreading past the edge and carrying the lift further than 2px

ak-neon-colour-glow.instead: a luminous glow tinted from the button's own fill, spreading softly past the edge and brightening the page under it

ak-faint-halo.instead: a glow that spreads visibly past the edge and reaches full strength on hover

ak-shortcut-ease-preset.instead: cubic-bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2) written out, the curve held in a custom property so each property takes its own

k-label-contrast.text: Does the label keep 4.5:1 contrast against the glow at its brightest point, on its plate or contrast layer?

test.spec: contrast ratio of the label colour against the composite behind it at full glow strength, 4.5 or more (3 for large text)

k-target-size.text: Is the clickable box at least 24 by 24 CSS px, with the glow left out of the measure?

test.spec: min-width and min-height of the button box, excluding the ::before glow layer

k-focus-ring.text: Does keyboard focus show a 3px ring offset from the edge that stays at 3:1 against the glow?

test.spec: focus-visible ring at 3px or more, offset from the edge, measured at 3:1 or more against the glow at full strength

k-compositor.text: Do the hover transitions animate only transform and opacity, with the glow built as a faded layer rather than a box-shadow?

test.spec: no transition declaration in :hover rules names top, left, width, height, margin, padding or box-shadow; the glow layer transitions opacity

k-cubic-bezier.text: Is every custom curve written as cubic-bezier() with x1 and x2 inside 0 to 1?

test.spec: in each cubic-bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2), x1 and x2 lie between 0 and 1, while y values may leave that range

k-hover-default-ease.text: Does the hover use a hand-written curve rather than the default ease keyword?

test.spec: a transition on :hover that names bare ease, ease-in or ease-out without a cubic-bezier() is a match

k-dreamlike-motion.text: Does the hover keep moving in the shape its reading names (a settle with a long tail, a float held while the pointer rests, a slow enter, or a breath), rather than snapping to rest?

test.spec: in the hovered state, the chosen reading still changes after the value would look finished: a settle still moving about 600ms after it would stop, or a float or breath still looping while held

k-glow-spreads.text: Does the glow spread past the edge and gain strength to full hover, rather than sit as a faint halo?

test.spec: glow visibly beyond the box edge at full hover strength

k-reverse-mid-hover.text: When the pointer leaves mid-settle, does the glow reverse from its current value instead of jumping to rest?

test.spec: sample the glow opacity a few frames after mouseleave: it falls from the value reached, with no step back to rest

k-practical.text: Do the label, the focus ring, the target and the press state all still work with the glow and motion at full strength?

test.spec: at full glow strength: label passes 4.5:1 on its plate or contrast layer, focus ring passes 3:1 against the glow, the box is 24 by 24 CSS px, and press feedback shows before the hover curve finishes

k-reduced-motion.text: Under prefers-reduced-motion, does the hover keep its colour and glow response and drop the travel and the loop?

test.spec: emulate prefers-reduced-motion: reduce and compare computed transform and animation-name on hover

k-touch-hover.text: On a tap, does the button leave no hover stuck on?

test.spec: hover effects are gated by a hover-capable media query, and the press state gives the tap feedback

oq-penner-values.text: Control points for the Penner-style named families (out, in-out, back, anticipation) were not retrieved; the families are spreads in cf-spread.

oq-overshoot-in-guide.text: The Josh Comeau transitions guide does not cover overshoot; overshoot values come from MDN only (cf-overshoot).

oq-hover-not-in-mdn.text: The MDN prefers-reduced-motion page does not discuss hover; the hover fallback (rm-hover) is inferred from the reduce keyword.
oq-hover-not-in-mdn.impact: how hover is treated under reduced motion

request._about: The user's words, verbatim, one entry per clause. The prompt sets the scope; these entries stay as wide as written.

rq-button.text: The prompt asks for a button.

rq-bezier-hover.term: custom bezier curve hover state animations
rq-bezier-hover.anchor: custom bezier curve hover state animations
rq-bezier-hover.text: The button has hover state animations that use custom bezier curves.

rq-dreamlike.text: The button makes it feel dreamlike and ethereal.

rq-practical.text: The button is practical for a website.

ux_principles._about: Discipline rungs: UI and interaction design, motion design for web interfaces. Inferred from practice; the accessibility rules are in accessibility_rules.

ux-feedback-timing.text: A control shows that it heard the pointer or key at once; response delays are read against rough time limits.
behaviors: A press with no visible change for about a second reads as broken
Motion that starts within a tenth of a second reads as directly caused by the input
ux-feedback-timing.principle: The user should always know the system heard the action and what it is doing.
signals: button changes state within 100 ms of input
no dead time before any response

ux-motion-easing.text: Easing shapes how a move feels: slow-out reads as arriving, slow-in as leaving, and a long tail reads as settling.
behaviors: An ease-out entrance feels responsive because the element moves fast first
A long tail that keeps drifting after the main move reads as soft and floating
Overshoot reads as springy and playful, and can make a control feel unstable at small sizes
ux-motion-easing.principle: The curve tells the eye whether an element is arriving, leaving or settling.
signals: fast start with slow end
motion stops gently rather than cutting

tokens.tail_share: most of the time in the last third

ux-fitts-hick-jakob.text: Three laws of interaction: time to reach a target grows with distance and falls with size, choices add decision time, and users expect familiar conventions.
behaviors: A larger, closer target is hit faster, so a button's active area matters as much as its look
A row of many similar buttons slows the pick; one clear primary action speeds it
A button that looks like a link or a standard button is understood without a learning step
ux-fitts-hick-jakob.principle: Make the likely action large, near where the eye already is, and recognisable at a glance.
signals: one primary button per group
pad the hit area beyond the visual edge

buttons._about: Rung: buttons and calls to action. Inferred from practice.

btn-states-feedback.term: button states and the hover-focus-press pattern
btn-states-feedback.text: A button has rest, hover, focus-visible, active (press) and disabled states. Each can read as its own state, and each can be reached without a pointer.
behaviors: Hover feedback shows on pointer devices; the same change can also happen on keyboard focus
The press state can respond instantly even when hover uses a slow curve, so the click never feels late
Disabled can look inert while its label stays legible enough to read
btn-states-feedback.principle: Every state the pointer reaches can also be reached from the keyboard.
signals: hover and focus-visible share one style
active state present
common_mistakes: Hover-only feedback: touch has no hover, keyboard users get nothing, and the button looks dead
Hover-only motion that is slow to start, so the first thing the user sees is a delay
Motion longer than the action it accompanies: the press finishes before the animation does

accessibility_rules._about: Rung: accessibility, WCAG 2.2. Each rule carries the quote from the W3C page it was fetched from.

a11y-motion-interaction.term: animation from interactions and reduced motion
a11y-motion-interaction.text: WCAG 2.3.3 (AAA) lets users disable motion triggered by interaction unless it is essential; prefers-reduced-motion is the CSS signal for that setting.
behaviors: Inside a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce query, the hover drift, glow pulse and lift are removed or replaced with an instant colour change
The focus ring and state colour still change, so reduced-motion users keep every signal except the movement
a11y-motion-interaction.principle: Motion is decoration on a button; the state change must still work without it.
signals: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block present
state readable with animation off

a11y-target-size.text: WCAG 2.5.8 (AA) asks pointer targets to be at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, or to keep 24 CSS pixels of spacing from neighbours.
a11y-target-size.invariant: the clickable area is at least 24 by 24 CSS px, or keeps 24 px clear of neighbouring targets
a11y-target-size.variable: visual box size, padding, the glow halo outside the box, spacing between buttons
behaviors: A visually small button can keep a 24 px hit area by padding the box, so the look stays slim
A glow or halo outside the box does not count toward the target; only the clickable box does
a11y-target-size.principle: Small targets are hard to hit for people with tremor or reduced precision.
signals: min-height and min-width at 24px or more
clickable box measured, not the glow

a11y-focus-visible.term: focus visible and focus not obscured
a11y-focus-visible.text: WCAG 2.4.7 (AA) needs a visible focus indicator; 2.4.11 (AA) needs the focused item at least partly on screen, not covered by other content.
a11y-focus-visible.invariant: a keyboard user can see which button has focus, and no other content covers the focus indicator
a11y-focus-visible.variable: ring colour, offset, shape, and whether the glow itself serves as the focus cue
behaviors: A dreamlike glow must not replace the focus ring: keyboard users need a crisp outline or equivalent
A floating or sticky element that covers the focused button fails 2.4.11, so scroll padding keeps it clear
:focus-visible draws the ring for keyboard focus and leaves pointer clicks clean
a11y-focus-visible.principle: Keyboard users must always see where they are.
signals: outline on :focus-visible
scroll-margin set on buttons

a11y-label-contrast.term: label contrast on glow and translucency
a11y-label-contrast.text: WCAG 1.4.3 (AA) asks text to reach 4.5:1 against its background; large text needs 3:1.
a11y-label-contrast.invariant: the label keeps readable contrast against whatever is behind it at the glow's brightest point
a11y-label-contrast.variable: glow colour, glow spread, blur radius, fill translucency, gradient hue, glow opacity
behaviors: The label keeps 4.5:1 against the glow at the brightest point of the glow, not only at rest
A translucent fill is judged against the actual page colour behind it, so the label is checked on the real backdrop
a11y-label-contrast.principle: The label must stay readable at the moment the glow is strongest.
signals: contrast checked at hover peak
label colour darkens or lightens against the glow

focus_ring_spread.text: The focus ring needs 3:1 against what it touches at focus, which is the glow: focus-visible sets the glow to opacity 1. WCAG 1.4.11 is not fetched in this dump.
behaviors: A dark ring on a dark page with no glow fails 3:1 (1.04:1); the glow carries its contrast
Which ring holds 3:1 depends on the page and the glow peak; see a11y-ring-colours
focus_ring_spread.principle: The ring is checked against what it touches at focus: the glow.
signals: ring visible on a dark page

tokens.method_note: 3:1 from WCAG 1.4.11 as known, needs a fetched source before tier 1

a11y-ring-colours.text: Illustrative 3px rings, offset 3px, measured against the glow peak on a white page and on a dark page.

tokens.method_note: computed from listed hex values; recompute on the real backdrop

css_motion._about: Syntax and states of CSS motion, sourced from MDN and WCAG. Control points only as the fetched pages give them.

cm-transition-vs-animation.text: A transition runs between two states, triggered by :hover, :active or JavaScript. An animation runs a named @keyframes sequence and needs no state change.
behaviors: Hover lift and glow use transition; a looping breathing glow uses animation
cm-transition-vs-animation.principle: Transition answers a state change; animation plays a sequence.

cm-keywords.text: Named keywords are fixed cubic-bezier curves: ease, ease-in, ease-out and ease-in-out. Use them as a baseline before writing custom curves.
behaviors: ease-out starts fast and settles slowly, which suits a hover that lands softly
ease-in-out suits looping motion; ease is the default when no timing function is given
linear keeps a constant pace

cm-cubic-bezier.text: Four numbers x1, y1, x2, y2 place the two middle control points; the curve is fixed from (0,0) to (1,1). x1 and x2 must be in [0, 1]; an invalid curve makes CSS drop the whole property.
behaviors: A bad x value silently removes the hover transition
Any named timing function can be replaced by a custom cubic-bezier value in the same declaration
signals: cubic-bezier( in a transition or animation declaration
transition: transform 250ms cubic-bezier(...)

examples.does: symmetric slow in and out: a breath

curve_families._about: Curve families and spreads. Control points come from the fetched MDN page only; open_questions hold what was not retrieved.

cf-overshoot.text: A y value above 1 makes the value pass its end state and return, a spring-like settle that can make a button look bouncy.
cf-overshoot.quote_note: MDN: can cause the value to go farther than the final state and then return
behaviors: Overshoot on a glow reads as a pop; on a lift it reads as a bounce
Overshoot on opacity can push the glow past full strength for a frame
signals: button moves past its resting spot and returns
brief brightness spike on the glow
cf-overshoot.principle: Overshoot adds a second event after the first; a soft settle keeps one.

cf-spread.text: Named families (Penner-style out, in-out, back, anticipation) are spreads to pick from, not fetched control points: soft settle, overshoot, anticipation.
behaviors: Anticipation starts by moving backward before going forward

performance._about: Which properties stay cheap while a button moves.

pf-compositor.text: Animate opacity and transform: they stay on the compositor, while top, left and layout properties drop frames.
behaviors: Lift with translate, glow with opacity on a pseudo-element

pf-blur-paint.text: Blur and shadow take longer to paint than a plain box. Animating box-shadow repaints each frame; a glow on a pseudo-element with opacity avoids that (inferred).
behaviors: Many glowing buttons on one page repaint together; limit glow to the hovered button
pf-blur-paint.principle: Paint cost scales with blurred area per frame.

heading_path: Glowing Effects on CSS Buttons using HTML & CSS

scr-glow-hover.text: On hover the glow fades in over 0.3s, and while pressed the background drops away and the blur tightens from 5px to 2px.
behaviors: Hover reveals the glow; pointer leaving fades it back out
Pressing sharpens the halo, so the press reads as a tightening
scr-glow-hover.principle: Reveal on hover, sharpen on press: the state change is carried by opacity and blur, not by moving the control.
signals: button:hover:before opacity 1
button:hover:active:before filter blur(2px)

scr-glow-look.term: glow at full strength on screen
scr-glow-look.text: In the page's hero image the glow is a saturated rainbow rim around a near-black button on black, reading as a lit edge rather than a drop shadow.
behaviors: The dark fill keeps the label legible while the rim carries the colour
Full strength makes the colour the subject, against a black field
scr-glow-look.principle: A dark body under a bright rim reads as emitted light.
signals: colour sits around the edge, not under the label
dark fill, bright halo

scr-glow-strength.term: faint halo to full glow spread
scr-glow-strength.text: The page's values are one point on a spread: opacity 0 to 1, blur 2px to 8px, gradient cycle 10s to 30s, each step trading brightness for softness.
behaviors: Low opacity and high blur reads as a faint halo
Full opacity and low blur reads as a hard neon rim
scr-glow-strength.principle: Strength and softness move together; the consumer picks the point on the spread.
signals: halo bleeds past the edge
rim hugs the edge

heading_path: Glowing Effects on CSS Buttons using HTML & CSS
Glowing Effect on Button using HTML & CSS [Source Codes]

scr-glow-build.text: The glow is a ::before pseudo-element behind the button, slightly larger than it, with a blurred multicolour gradient and opacity 0 at rest.
behaviors: The button's own background sits above the glow, so only the 2px-4px rim shows as halo
The gradient drifts across the 400% background as the animation runs
scr-glow-build.principle: The glow is a separate layer behind the control, so the control stays crisp and readable.
signals: z-index -1 on a pseudo-element
opacity transition, not a shadow

scr-blur-cost.term: blur cost on the glow layer
scr-blur-cost.text: A blur filter on an animating gradient layer repaints each frame, so the glow is the expensive part of this button, not the transition.
properties: filter blur on a moving layer
behaviors: Animating background-position repaints the blurred layer; a smaller blur radius costs less per frame
Small blur keeps a crisp rim; large blur spreads the light onto the page
scr-blur-cost.principle: The cost sits in the blurred animated layer, so that layer is where to trim first.
signals: janky hover on low-end devices
many blurred layers at once

does: 2: a crisp rim that tightens on press
5: the sourced default, a soft edge
8: a diffused cloud reaching the page

gl-isolation.text: The glow is a z-index -1 pseudo-element. A stacking context on the button keeps it between the page and the button's own box, instead of letting it fall behind a parent's background.
behaviors: Without a context, z-index -1 puts the glow behind the nearest ancestor that paints a background, which can hide it
With isolation, the glow stays inside the button's layer, above the page and below the button's own background
A z-index on a positioned button creates the same context; isolation is the explicit form
gl-isolation.principle: Layering works only inside a context, and the glow needs one to sit between the page and the label.
signals: glow missing on a section with a background
isolation or z-index on the button

feel._about: How a hover's enter and exit read in the guide.

tm-action-driven.text: A hover can give its enter and exit different transitions, so the press-in and the release feel like two events.
properties: symmetrical default uses one duration both ways
behaviors: Splitting enter from exit makes the hover read as mouse-enter and mouse-leave events instead of a state
signals: a transition set inside :hover that differs from the base transition

limits._about: What the guide says about extremes and gaps.

cb-limits.text: The guide points to an extended set of timing functions but warns that some of the more outlandish ones won't work in CSS.
signals: a curve that works in a design tool may not be valid in a transition

reduced_motion._about: What the prefers-reduced-motion setting asks of motion, and how a reduce fallback is written. Scraped from MDN.

rm-query.text: A device setting that tells the page the user wants less non-essential motion, so the page removes, reduces or replaces motion-based animation.
behaviors: reduce evaluates as true, so @media (prefers-reduced-motion) means the same as (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)
no-preference evaluates as false, so a page with no reduce block keeps its full motion
rm-query.principle: The user's device setting decides whether motion is reduced, not the page's own default.
signals: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block in the stylesheet

rm-triggers.text: Scaling and panning large objects are the motion most likely to trigger discomfort for readers with vestibular motion disorders.
behaviors: A pulsing box that scales in size is the example the page uses for a trigger
A change in opacity without movement is named as the muted alternative
rm-triggers.principle: Large, travelling movement is what the setting exists to remove; small or fading change is the usual replacement.
signals: transform: scale or translate on a large element
keyframes that move a large area

rm-hover.text: Applying the same rule to a hover transition: the reduce block keeps the colour or glow change and drops the travel, such as a lift by translate or a scale.
behaviors: A hover that lifts the button by transform keeps its colour change and loses the lift under reduce
A glow that changes only opacity or colour survives the reduce block unchanged
rm-hover.principle: The muted alternative keeps the response to the pointer and drops the movement across the screen.
signals: transform removed inside the reduce block for :hover
transition-duration kept for colour

hover_motion._about: Motion side of the hover: readings of dreamlike, a pool of curves per reading, duration spreads, decision points and options. Pick from the pool; nothing here is a finished set.

curve_pool._about: Exemplar curves per reading, labeled illustrative. Several per reading, far apart; pick one per property or hold them as custom properties. Durations are starting points.

cp-enter-slow.text: Slow start that arrives late: 8% of the travel by a quarter of the time, half by the middle, then a soft landing. It makes the hover arrive rather than respond; for a quick answer use cp-settle-short.

cp-float-sine.text: Symmetric sine-like in-out for a gentle loop; the second curve gives a rounder start with a pause at the top.

cp-float-linear.text: Near-linear pace keeps a steady drift to the top; the second curve front-loads the drift.

cp-settle-long.text: Expo-like ease-out with a long low tail; the second curve is a standard decelerate that lands sooner.

cp-settle-short.text: Quadratic-like ease-out that lands sooner, for a tail with less float; the second curve is a gentler quad out.

cp-breath-sine.text: Even rise and fall, which reads as breath; the second curve rises slower than it falls.

cp-breath-uneven.text: Slow rise, quick fall: the glow gathers and releases; the second curve is a looser swell.

cp-magnet-snap.text: Quick follow that stays close to the pointer; the second curve eases in and out.

cp-magnet-overshoot.text: Follows with a small overshoot on the way back to centre; the second curve is a back ease with a larger overshoot.

opt-rest-glow.text: A low-opacity glow at rest that grows on hover, so the button reads as lit before the pointer arrives.

opt-press-tighten.text: On press the glow's pre-rendered blur layer fades its opacity down and the lift goes flat, with transform and opacity only. Nothing animates filter on press, so the press stays smooth on mid-range phones.

hm-settle-shape.term: settle shape: front, late, or slow start
hm-settle-shape.text: Where the time is spent decides how the move reads. Three shapes sit side by side, each with what it does.
behaviors: Fast front with a long low tail arrives at once, then floats on: the tail carries the feel
Slow start with a late arrival drifts in and lands at the end: it reads as arriving
Symmetric in-out rises and falls evenly: it reads as a glide
hm-settle-shape.principle: Pick the shape per button or per property: arrive and float, or drift in and arrive late.

hm-durations.term: duration spread: quick enter, slow enter, slow exit
hm-durations.text: Enter and exit can run at different speeds. Quick feedback lands in 120 to 250ms, a slow arrival takes 1.2 to 2.4s, and the exit runs 250 to 450ms. The feel of a slow arrival is in hm-settle-shape.
behaviors: A quick enter under about 250ms reads as the button answering the pointer

hm-interruption.text: A pointer that leaves mid-enter needs a reversal rule. Three options side by side. Sourced press and focus timing sit in press_focus; the reversal fact is in reverse-mid-transition.

look._about: The look of the button at rest, hover and press: the glow, fill and edge layers, and the exemplar pool. Values are spreads, not settings.

look-exemplars._about: Exemplar pool, one or two per reading, labeled by the reading each serves. Illustrative.

look-label-contrast.text: A translucent fill can stay if a layer between the glow and the label holds 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text) at the glow's peak: a solid plate, a text-shadow halo or a frosted inner ring.
behaviors: A solid plate behind the label only: the fill stays translucent around it
A text-shadow halo has no fixed ratio; measure the label on the composite behind it
A frosted inner ring is a 1px inset edge; it does not count as the label's background
A dark label on a 0.2 fill holds its ratio at the glow peak; a light label on a dark page does not

practical._about: What has to keep working for the button to be practical. Each invariant names its variable, what is free to change. None caps how dreamlike the hover gets. Label contrast, target size and focus are in accessibility_rules with their variables.

pr-touch-hover.invariant: touch users get a working press and result without depending on a hover that a tap cannot produce
pr-touch-hover.variable: which hover effects are gated, whether the glow shows on :active, the tap feedback
pr-touch-hover.text: A tap has no hover, and a hover left on after a tap can stick. Gating hover behind a hover-capable pointer lets touch users rely on the press state.
behaviors: Hover gated by a hover-capable media query does not stick after a tap
A glow shown on :active gives touch users the same light as hover
pr-touch-hover.principle: Hover belongs to pointers; the press belongs to every device.
signals: glow stuck on after a tap

pr-smooth-motion.invariant: the hover runs at frame rate on a mid-range device, and a page with many buttons stays smooth
pr-smooth-motion.variable: which properties move, how the glow is built, how many buttons glow at once, the curve and duration
pr-smooth-motion.text: Move transform and opacity. Keep blur and shadow fixed on a pseudo-element and fade its opacity. The glow runs on the hovered button, not across the whole page.
behaviors: Animating top or left drops frames far more than transform does
Animating box-shadow repaints every frame
A fixed blurred layer with an opacity transition avoids repaint
pr-smooth-motion.principle: The compositor moves layers cheaply; paint is what costs frames.
signals: jank on hover

pr-screen-reader.invariant: the accessible name stays the visible label, and the glow, gradient and halo are not read out
pr-screen-reader.variable: any decorative layer, its markup, and any pseudo-element content
pr-screen-reader.text: Glow layers are decoration: pseudo-elements with empty content, and decorative icons marked aria-hidden. The name then comes only from the label.
behaviors: A pseudo-element with text content can be announced as part of the name
An empty glow layer adds nothing to the name
pr-screen-reader.principle: The name is the label; everything drawn around it stays out of the name.

pr-reduced-motion.text: Choose one fallback per button: keep colour and glow and drop the travel, a static glow, a short opacity fade, or an instant change.

press_focus._about: Press, focus and contrast facts for the button's :active and :focus-visible states. Researched facts are quoted; what they mean for this button is inferred.

press-timing.text: Desktop state changes should be short and immediately responsive; Material's desktop range is 150 to 200 ms.
behaviors: A press or hover change inside 150 to 200 ms reads as a direct response on desktop
Shorter exit or return motion is fine because leaving needs less attention (inferred for the return path)
press-timing.principle: Keep state changes short, since users see them often.
signals: state change finishes inside about 200 ms on desktop

press-active-fast.text: A community skill file suggests about 50 ms ease-out for press feedback; no official standard was found, so treat it as a lead.
behaviors: A scale-down on :active near 0.97 reads as a press without a long transition
signals: pressed state visible before the finger or pointer lifts

focus-visible-rule.text: Show the focus ring for keyboard focus through :focus-visible, separate from pointer hover.
behaviors: A hover glow on a mouse click does not need to double as the focus ring
The focus ring can fade in on keyboard focus only; its duration is not sourced, so pick a value inside the press range (inferred)
signals: ring appears on Tab and not on mouse click

focus-contrast-3to1.text: Focus indicators need 3:1 against adjacent colours, so a glow or colour shift used as the focus ring must be checked against the rest state.
behaviors: A focus ring that is only a faint glow on a pale page can fail even when it is visible
The label must keep its contrast under the glow (inferred; see the label contrast entry)
focus-contrast-3to1.principle: Focus must be visible without relying on the hover effect alone.
signals: focus ring measured at 3:1 or more against adjacent colour

interruption._about: How a hover or press that changes mid-transition behaves. The reversal rule comes from a search snippet of the CSS Transitions Level 2 spec and was not read from a fetched page.

reverse-mid-transition.text: A reversed CSS transition starts from the value it has reached, and the spec shortens the reverse so the return is faster than a full run.
behaviors: Moving the pointer off during a slow glow rise makes the return start from the current glow, not jump to rest
A long hover curve reverses at a shorter time, so a slow drift still feels responsive when the pointer leaves
reverse-mid-transition.principle: Reversal continues from the current value, so a cut-short hover looks continuous.
signals: no visible jump when the pointer leaves mid-hover

press-stuck.text: The :active state lasts only while the pointer or finger is held, so a press transition longer than a click can lag or stick after release. Source is a forum answer, so it is a lead, not a rule.
behaviors: A slow press transition on touch can still be finishing when the finger lifts
signals: pressed styling still visible after release
